sentence: This project builds tools and techniques for making genetically modified marmosets that can be used as models of brain function.
This project uses machine learning to study rare noncoding variants and tries to link genes to Alzheimer's disease risk.
This project develops preventive and compensatory measures that aim to improve quality of life in an aging population.
This project stores brain imaging data, checks its quality, and builds analysis pipelines to measure brain structure, function, and connectivity across subjects and time.
This project studies how changes in glycosylation affect proteins and disease, and builds methods to see and characterize glycans and glycoproteins in tissues.
This project studies how a gene contributes to leukemic cell proliferation in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
This project makes radionuclides and puts them into radiolabeled pharmaceuticals for imaging and therapy in research and patient use.
This project prepares a gene therapy that edits a mutation causing a smooth muscle disease that leads to strokes in children.
This project studies how lung cancer that has lost a particular gene resists immunotherapy and grows.
This project builds machine learning models to find rare noncoding variants that change gene regulation during heart development.
This project offers imaging, microscopy and tissue services that support cancer research.
This project tests whether a personalized oxygen-saturation target lowers mortality in critically ill adults receiving mechanical ventilation.
This project studies how the nasal pit forms and how this shapes upper lip formation and cleft lip.
This project studies how heroin changes mitochondrial biology and metabolism in the brain.
This project builds tools to track what happens to truncated transcripts in cancer cells across parts of the cell.
This project studies how inflammation and oxidation drive secondary cataract after cataract surgery.
This project collects and shares MRI scans and other brain imaging data to better understand what drives clinical progression of Alzheimer's disease.
This project offers microscopes and tissue staining services that let cancer researchers image and analyze cells and tissues.
This project studies how a signaling pathway controls lipopolysaccharide changes in Porphyromonas gingivalis that contribute to periodontitis.
This project tests whether acquired mutations are present in disease-related pathways in people with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
